title: SDK + docs: add canonical retry guidance for overload errors (Retry-After, exponential backoff + jitter)
creator: Ibrahim Khan
project: Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding (Reliability Program)
description:
## Context
Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding introduces new customer-visible overload semantics (ADR-014). We need to update SDK examples and docs snippets so customers:
- treat overload responses as *expected* under saturation
- avoid retry storms
- respect Retry-After
- use exponential backoff + jitter
- understand which errors are retryable vs not

This ticket covers:
- Docs site examples (Python + TypeScript) for handling overload errors
- SDK snippet updates (or references) to keep behavior consistent and reduce Support load

Out of scope:
- Changing the SDK default retry behavior globally (we’ll provide helper + examples; automatic retries remain opt-in)

## Requirements / Acceptance criteria
1) Docs page (Hosted API) includes a “Retry contract” section:
   - Which HTTP statuses are retryable: 429 / 503 overload
   - Which are *not* retryable: 400/401/403/404; 422 validation; 429 quota exhausted (distinct error code); 503 dependency-down if code indicates non-transient
   - Must explicitly say: “Do not retry immediately; always backoff + jitter; cap retries; honor Retry-After.”

2) Example code for Python + TypeScript:
   - Parse Retry-After header (seconds); if present, sleep that duration (with small jitter) before retry
   - If missing, fall back to exponential backoff + full jitter (or equal jitter), bounded by max delay
   - Respect request id / correlation id in logs (x-request-id / x-correlation-id) and surface stable overload error code
   - Handle streaming routes guidance: retry only if stream did not produce any tokens (idempotency caveat)

3) Examples must align with ADR-014 error fields and naming:
   - stable overload error code (e.g., overload.*)
   - include correlation_id / request_id
   - include Retry-After semantics

4) Provide a short “copy/paste” snippet for each SDK that Support can link.

## Links
- ADR-014: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-014-hosted-overload-error-taxonomy.json
- SDK PRs:
  - Python: sources/github/redwood-sdk-python/pr-621-handle-overload-errors-and-retry-after.json
  - TypeScript: sources/github/redwood-sdk-typescript/pr-418-expose-overload-error-types.json
- Gateway consistent Retry-After work: sources/github/redwood/pr-18472-load-shedding-retry-after-and-client-guidance.json
- Support guidance draft: sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/overload-errors-and-retry-guidance.json
- Docs plan ticket: sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/hosted-api-overload-errors-doc-update.json

## Proposed retry guidance (docs canonical)
### Retryable
- HTTP 429 when error code indicates overload / admission control (NOT quota exhausted)
- HTTP 503 when error code indicates overload / capacity saturation

### Non-retryable (examples)
- Invalid params / auth / permission: 400/401/403/404/422
- 429 when error code indicates quota / rate limit exceeded for plan (retrying immediately will not help)

### Algorithm
- Always prefer server guidance:
  - If Retry-After present: sleep Retry-After (+ 0–250ms jitter)
  - Else: backoff = min(max_delay, base * 2^attempt) and apply jitter
- Cap:
  - max attempts (e.g., 5)
  - max total retry time (e.g., 30s)
- Use idempotency:
  - If client can provide an idempotency key, recommend it for non-streaming requests
  - For streaming: recommend retry only if no tokens were received; otherwise surface partial output and let app decide

## Notes / gotchas
- Ensure examples don’t encourage synchronized retries.
- If we recommend 503 retries, emphasize respecting Retry-After to avoid thundering herd.
- Include a short log line example that prints overload error code + request id + region/model.

## Deliverables
- Docs snippets committed and linked from overload errors page
- SDK README / docs section updated to point to canonical retry helper
- Support-ready snippet (same code) to paste into replies
